sentiment.rationale: The company reported Q1 sales and EPS in line with expectations, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed unchanged. Management expressed confidence in their Total Home strategy and noted some positive trends (Pro growth, online growth), but also acknowledged ongoing pressure from DIY discretionary demand, a cautious consumer, and macro uncertainty. The forward outlook is essentially flat with no material change in expectations, warranting a neutral score.

summary.revenue: Q1 sales of $20.9 billion, comparable sales down 1.7%.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $2.92, in line with expectations.
summary.guidance: Affirmed fiscal 2025 outlook: sales $83.5B-$84.5B, comp sales flat to up 1%, operating margin 12.3%-12.4%, diluted EPS ~$12.15-$12.40. Q2 comp sales expected ~150 bps above bottom end of full-year guide.
summary.margin: Gross margin 33.4%, up 19 bps YoY. Operating margin 11.9%, down 50 bps YoY. Full-year gross margin expected roughly flat.
key_risks: Ongoing pressure in DIY bigger ticket discretionary demand.
Slower start to spring due to unfavorable weather.
Macro uncertainty and cautious consumer sentiment.
Elevated mortgage rates (~7%) affecting housing market.
Tariff impacts expected to be more concentrated in second half of the year.
Pro customers feeling less confident due to uncertain macro environment.
key_opportunities: Mid-single-digit Pro sales growth in Q1, driven by loyalty program and strategy.
Online sales up 6% with traffic and conversion gains.
Acquisition of Artisan Design Group to expand Pro penetration in new home construction.
Launch of product marketplace with Mirakl to scale extended aisle.
AI-powered Mylow virtual advisor and Mylow Companion for associates.
Strong spring in-stock positions and customer satisfaction scores up 100 bps.

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management expressed confidence in execution and strategy ('I'm pleased with our team's focus and execution') but also acknowledged headwinds ('ongoing challenges in the housing market', 'DIY bigger ticket discretionary demand remains under pressure').

evidence.claim: Q1 sales were $20.9 billion with comparable sales down 1.7%.
evidence.quote: In the first quarter, we delivered sales of $20.9 billion with comparable sales down 1.7%, in line with our expectations.

evidence.claim: Diluted EPS was $2.92, in line with expectations.
evidence.quote: Diluted earnings per share of $2.92 were in line with our expectations.

today we are affirming our fiscal 2025 outlook. We continue to expect sales ranging from $83.5 billion to $84.5 billion with comparable sales in a range of flat to up 1%. We expect operating margin in a range of 12.3% to 12.4% and full year diluted earnings per share of approximately $12.15 to $12.40.

evidence.claim: Gross margin was 33.4%, up 19 bps YoY.
evidence.quote: Gross margin was 33.4% of sales in the first quarter, up 19 basis points from last year, driven by multiple PPI initiatives as well as some modest improvement in Shrink and Credit revenue.

evidence.claim: Operating margin was 11.9%, down 50 bps YoY.
evidence.quote: Operating margin rate of 11.9% declined 50 basis points versus prior year and the effective tax rate was 23.9% in line with prior year.

evidence.claim: DIY bigger ticket discretionary demand remains under pressure.
evidence.quote: our financial results also reflect ongoing pressure in DIY bigger ticket discretionary demand and a slower start to spring versus last year with exceptionally unfavorable weather across much of the country in February.

evidence.claim: Pro sales grew mid-single digits in Q1.
evidence.quote: I'll begin with our mid-single-digit growth in Pro sales this quarter.
In the first quarter, online sales were up 6% driven by increases in both traffic and conversion rates.
I'm pleased with our team's focus and execution in the face of significant macro uncertainty... our financial results also reflect ongoing pressure in DIY bigger ticket discretionary demand.

evidence.claim: Tariff impacts expected to be more concentrated in second half.
evidence.quote: we do expect any incremental impact that we see to be more concentrated in the second half of our year, and that's baked into the expectation.

evidence.claim: Pro customers are feeling less confident.
evidence.quote: In our most recent survey, Pros indicated that project backlogs remain healthy, but they are feeling a little less confident as might be expected, given the uncertain macro environment.

evidence.claim: Acquisition of Artisan Design Group to expand Pro penetration.
evidence.quote: we announced a deal in April to acquire Artisan Design Group, or ADG, which is a leading provider of design, distribution, and installation services for interior surface finishes... We expect this acquisition to increase our penetration of Pro planned spend and will position us to gain share in a highly fragmented $50 billion market.

evidence.claim: Launch of product marketplace with Mirakl.
evidence.quote: we recently partnered with Mirakl, a global leader in marketplace technology to help us scale even faster. Through Mirakl, trusted marketplace sellers will be able to easily manage their catalogs on lowes.com.
In collaboration with Open AI, we launched Mylow, the first AI-powered Home Improvement Virtual Advisor.

Their efforts are paying off with customer satisfaction scores up 100 basis points over last year, as we leverage better technology and ongoing process improvements to enhance the shopping experience.

review_flags.reason: Score is 0.00 despite some positive operational momentum (Pro growth, online growth) and reaffirmed guidance. The neutral score reflects the lack of a guidance raise and acknowledged headwinds, but a reviewer may consider a slightly positive score given the organic momentum in Pro and online.
